title: GOING SHOPPING
conversation: Amy is at a clothing store shopping for a new pair of pants. Lisa, a saleswoman, asks her if she needs any help. Lisa: May I help you? Amy: I'm just browsing. Lisa: Let me know if I can help. My name is Lisa. Amy: Do these pants come in black? Lisa: Yes, but we're sold out. They're so popular, we can't keep them in stock. Amy: Do you have any black pants on sale? Lisa: Yes, these are marked down from $69.95 to $24.95. Amy: That's a good buy, but I'm not crazy about the fabric. Lisa: What about these pants? These are on sale for $49. Amy: That's a little pricey, but I'll try them on. (Amy enters the fitting room with the pants. A few minutes later, Lisa comes to check on her.) Lisa: How are the pants? Amy: A little snug. Lisa: That style does run small. Let me bring you the next size up. (Lisa hands Amy the pants and Amy puts them on.) Amy: These pants are a little big, aren't they? Lisa: No, they fit nicely! Amy: They're baggy in the back, don't you think? Lisa: No, they're perfect. Take my word for it. Amy: I'm just not sure. I think I'd better hold off for now.

idioms.meaning_en: shopping, without necessarily buying anything; only looking.
idioms.meaning_vi: chỉ đang xem qua (không có ý định mua ngay)
idioms.example: The clerk asked if I needed help, but I told her I was just browsing.
idioms.fill_sentence: Sarah loved visiting the local artisan market on weekends. She wasn't looking for anything specific to buy, but simply enjoyed seeing all the unique handmade items. When a vendor asked if she needed assistance, Sarah cheerfully replied, "I'm just browsing, thank you!" She moved from stall to stall, admiring the pottery, textiles, and jewelry, content to simply appreciate the craftsmanship without making a purchase.

idioms.meaning_en: To be produced or available in a certain color, size, or style.
idioms.meaning_vi: có sẵn (theo màu sắc, kích cỡ, kiểu dáng)
idioms.example: Does this dress come in a smaller size?
idioms.context: Do these pants come in black?
idioms.fill_sentence: I'm really interested in the new electric car model. I love its sleek design and the reported battery range. Does it come in any other colors besides the metallic blue? I'd really prefer a classic black or a deep red if possible. I should check the manufacturer's website for all available options.

idioms.example: I wanted to buy the new iPhone, but the store was completely sold out.
idioms.fill_sentence: My favorite band announced a new tour, and I was so excited to get tickets. I logged on right when they went on sale, but within minutes, all the tickets were completely gone. It seems the show was already sold out, so I'll have to wait for another opportunity.

idioms.meaning_en: Available for sale and present in the store.
idioms.example: We don't have any more of these shoes in stock right now.
idioms.context: They're so popular, we can't keep them in stock.
idioms.fill_sentence: Maria went to the electronics store hoping to buy the new smartphone. She asked the sales associate if they had any left. The associate quickly checked their system and confirmed that the phone was still in stock, much to Maria's relief. She was glad she wouldn't have to wait for a new shipment.

idioms.meaning_en: Offered at a lower price than usual / at a reduced price
idioms.example: I bought these jeans while they were on sale for 50% off.
idioms.context: Do you have any black pants on sale?
idioms.fill_sentence: I've been eyeing that new coffee machine for weeks, but its original price was just too high for my budget. My patience paid off, however, because I just saw an advertisement. Starting tomorrow, the exact model I want will be on sale, saving me a significant amount of money.

idioms.meaning_en: Reduced in price, lowered in price
idioms.example: All winter coats have been marked down to make room for spring clothes.
idioms.context: Yes, these are marked down from $69.95 to $24.95.
idioms.fill_sentence: David had been eyeing a new drone for months, but the original price was far too steep for his budget. He decided to wait until after the holiday rush, hoping for some post-season discounts. To his delight, a week later, the exact model he wanted was clearly marked down by 30% on the store's website. He quickly added it to his cart, thrilled to finally afford it at a reduced cost.

idioms.example: At only $10, that shirt is definitely a good buy.
idioms.context: That's a good buy, but I'm not crazy about the fabric.
idioms.fill_sentence: My old car was on its last legs, so I'd been saving up for a replacement. I spent weeks comparing prices and features, hoping to find a great deal. When the dealership offered a significant discount on the model I wanted, I knew instantly it was a good buy. I drove it home feeling incredibly satisfied with the bargain.

idioms.meaning_en: To not like or enjoy something very much; to not be enthusiastic about.
idioms.example: I'm not crazy about spicy food, so let's eat somewhere else.
idioms.context: That's a good buy, but I'm not crazy about the fabric.
idioms.fill_sentence: The company picnic always features a lively karaoke competition, and everyone gets really enthusiastic. While I enjoy the camaraderie, I'm not crazy about performing in front of a big crowd. I prefer to clap along from the back rather than grab the microphone myself and risk sounding terrible.

idioms.example: The food was delicious, but the restaurant was a little pricey.
idioms.context: That's a little pricey, but I'll try them on.
idioms.fill_sentence: My classmates wanted to study at the new aesthetic café near our campus because of its high-speed internet. However, we quickly noticed that a single cup of matcha latte cost three times the normal rate, making the menu quite pricey for students on a tight budget. We decided to stick to our usual local street vendor instead to save money.

idioms.meaning_en: To put on clothing to see if it fits.
idioms.example: You should try them on before you buy them.
idioms.context: That's a little pricey, but I'll try them on.
idioms.fill_sentence: If you are unsure of your size at the clothing store, you shouldn't just guess. It is always best to go to the changing room and try something on to see if it fits your body shape. This will save you the trouble of having to return a tight shirt later.

idioms.example: These shoes are a little snug; do you have a larger size?
idioms.fill_sentence: I bought a pair of leather boots in my usual size, but when I wore them with thick winter socks, they felt a little snug around my toes. Fortunately, the store assistant assured me that the leather would stretch and mold to my feet after a few days of wear.

idioms.meaning_en: to fit small / to fit large (a cut or style of clothing that is smaller or bigger than expected)
idioms.meaning_vi: cỡ hơi nhỏ (so với tiêu chuẩn thông thường)
idioms.example: Italian designer clothes often run small.
idioms.fill_sentence: When shopping on this international website, you cannot always trust the standard size labels. Some shoes run small / run big depending on the country of manufacture, so you must read the customer reviews to know whether to order a size up or down.

idioms.meaning_en: Believe me; trust what I say.
idioms.example: It's a great movie, just take my word for it.
idioms.context: No, they're perfect. Take my word for it.
idioms.fill_sentence: The tiny noodle shop down this alley doesn't have any signboards, menus, or online reviews, so you will just have to take my word for it that their beef pho is incredible. I have eaten there for five years and know the owner personally, so you can trust my recommendation.

idioms.meaning_en: To delay or wait before doing something.
idioms.example: We should hold off on buying a new car until next year.
idioms.context: I think I'd better hold off for now.
idioms.fill_sentence: Minh wanted to buy a new laptop today because his old one is extremely slow. However, his friend told him that a major tech sale starts next Monday with 50% discounts. To save a large amount of money, Minh decided to hold off until the promotion begins.
